judge_assessment.explanation: I confirmed the judge's recomputation directly from the TikZ in worksheet.tex rather than from the rendered page: problem 1 draws 3 dots, problem 2 draws 5 (four corners plus centre), problem 3 fills 4 of 5 frame cells, problem 4 fills 2, problem 5 draws 2+2, problem 6 draws 3+2, problem 7 is a square of 4 against a slant of 3 so '>', and problem 8 is two boxes of 2 against a full five-frame so '<'. That is exactly the judge's list of 3, 5, 4, 2, 4, 5, >, <. The study guide's four try-its (4-shape, 5-2=3 ... printed checks 3, 4, 5, '>') are likewise correct, and the small-type / three-page observation is fair. The judge missed one thing: Quick Answers entries 7 and 8 print '---' rather than the verified '>' and '<', so a quarter of the grading bank is blank. ACCEPT remains correct.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is a real perceptual trap rather than a decorative one. The left card is two separate boxes holding 2+2=4 and the right is a single compact full five-frame holding 5; the wider-looking card holds fewer. Both the key and the delivery note name this as the design intent, and it is the misconception (area for quantity) that K.CC.B.4 exists to break.

The answer key opens with a usage note no CAS could have produced: 'a child who counts one-by-one and gets the right number, the answer is correct but the target skill is not yet there -- flash the card for about two seconds and ask again.' For a subitizing sheet, that note is the assessment instrument; the numbers alone cannot distinguish subitizing from counting.
No numeral is printed on any dot card or five-frame, so the picture really is the number and the figures cannot leak the answer -- worksheet.tex confirms every card is bare TikZ circles.

root_causes.description: Same relation-rendering hole as elsewhere in the run: scripts/render_quick_answers.py._fmt() sympifies string expecteds, and a bare '>' or '<' falls into the '---' fallback that the module documents as 'manual-only / see solution'.

improvements.title: Quick Answers bank prints an em-dash instead of the verified > / < relation
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, _fmt() sends every string 'expected' through sympy.sympify(); '>' and '<' raise SympifyError and fall through to the '---' branch, which the module's own docstring reserves for 'see solution' / manual-only ids. Add a relation branch before the sympify attempt: map the bare relation tokens ('>', '<', '>=', '<=', '=', '≥', '≤') to their math-mode LaTeX ($>$, $<$, $\ge$, $\le$, $=$) and return that. Everything else keeps its current behaviour, so genuinely manual ids still print '---' and remain distinguishable from a verified relation.
improvements.regression_test: Add a case to tests/test_render_quick_answers.py that renders a verify JSON containing {"id": 1, "type": "compare", "values": ["5+3", "4+2"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"} alongside a {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry, and asserts the bank line for id 1 contains '$>$' while the line for id 2 is '---'. It fails today because both render '---'.
improvements.expected_impact: Every worksheet whose verification_targets include 'compare' with order 'relation' regains real entries in the grader's at-a-glance bank. In this shard alone that is curr-002 (2 of 10 entries), curr-006 (2 of 8), curr-032 (2 of 10), curr-038 (part of entry 8) and curr-050 (2 of 10).
improvements.risk: Low and contained to the bank. The entries are plain text by design and are never read by check_answer_key.py, so the strict per-problem binding gate cannot be affected. Only risk is choosing a LaTeX spelling that does not compile, which the existing compile-ak gate would catch immediately.

case_summary: A focused, correct subitizing sheet. The four-strategy structure (named dot pattern, five-frame read by its empty cells, two small groups composed, then comparison) matches the study guide section for section, difficulty ramps 1,1,2,2,2,3,3,4, and the figures were authored so that nothing on the page states a number. Every worksheet and study-guide value recomputes correctly against the TikZ. Only defect found: the Quick Answers bank blanks the two relation answers. One judgement call I want to record as sound rather than as a defect -- the standards tag is the broad K.CC.A.1-K.CC.C.7 row instead of the contract's narrower K.CC.B.4-K.CC.B.5, because references/standards-map.md carries only the single wide 'Counting & cardinality' row, and the delivery note says so explicitly rather than inventing a code.
